tasks.title: Create Core Organization, Membership, and Invitation Models
tasks.description: Establish the foundational database schema and models for multi-tenancy. This includes creating the Organization, OrganizationMembership, and Invitation models, and updating the User model to support these new relationships as outlined in PRD Phase 1.
tasks.details: Generate migrations for `organizations`, `organization_memberships`, and `invitations` tables using UUIDs for primary keys. Implement model associations (e.g., `has_many :users, through: :memberships`), validations, and role-based logic using Rails enums for the `role` field. Add `has_secure_token` to the Invitation model for secure token generation. Update the User model with `has_many :organizations, through: :memberships`.
tasks.testStrategy: Write RSpec model tests for each new model. For Organization, test validations and slug generation. For OrganizationMembership, test the role enum, scopes, and uniqueness constraints. For Invitation, test token generation, expiration logic, and the `accept` method. Update User model tests to verify the new associations.

subtasks.title: Generate Organization Model and Migration
subtasks.description: Create the migration for the `organizations` table and the corresponding `Organization` model. This will be the central model for multi-tenancy.
subtasks.details: Run `rails g model Organization name:string slug:string:uniq`. In the generated migration file, ensure the primary key is a UUID by setting `id: :uuid`. Add a `NOT NULL` constraint to the `name` column. In the `app/models/organization.rb` file, add `validates :name, presence: true`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Write a model spec for Organization. Test that a new organization is invalid without a name. Verify that saving a valid organization automatically generates a unique slug.

subtasks.title: Generate OrganizationMembership Model and Migration
subtasks.description: Create the join model and table to connect Users and Organizations, which will also store the member's role.
subtasks.details: Run `rails g model OrganizationMembership role:integer`. In the migration, add `t.references :user, null: false, foreign_key: true, type: :uuid` and `t.references :organization, null: false, foreign_key: true, type: :uuid`. Ensure the primary key is `id: :uuid`. Add a unique index on `[:user_id, :organization_id]`. In `app/models/organization_membership.rb`, add `belongs_to :user` and `belongs_to :organization`. Define an enum for the role: `enum role: { admin: 0, member: 1 }, _default: :member`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Write a model spec for OrganizationMembership. Test the uniqueness constraint for a user and organization pair. Verify the `role` enum defaults to 'member' and correctly handles assignment and querying for 'admin' and 'member' roles.

subtasks.title: Update User and Organization Models with Associations
subtasks.description: Wire up the many-to-many relationships between Users and Organizations through the new OrganizationMembership model.
subtasks.details: In `app/models/organization.rb`, add `has_many :organization_memberships, dependent: :destroy` and `has_many :users, through: :organization_memberships`. In `app/models/user.rb`, add `has_many :organization_memberships, dependent: :destroy` and `has_many :organizations, through: :organization_memberships`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Update the User model spec. Create a user and two organizations, associate the user with both via memberships, and assert that `user.organizations.count` is 2. Do the same for the Organization model spec, associating two users with one organization.

subtasks.title: Generate Invitation Model and Migration
subtasks.description: Create the model and migration for handling invitations for users to join an organization.
subtasks.details: Run `rails g model Invitation email:string:uniq role:integer token:string:uniq:index`. In the migration, ensure `id: :uuid`. Add `t.references :organization, null: false, foreign_key: true, type: :uuid` and `t.references :invited_by, null: false, foreign_key: { to_table: :users }, type: :uuid`. In `app/models/invitation.rb`, add `has_secure_token`, `belongs_to :organization`, and `belongs_to :invited_by, class_name: 'User'`. Add `validates :email, presence: true`. Define the same role enum as in `OrganizationMembership`.
subtasks.testStrategy: Write a model spec for Invitation. Test that a token is automatically generated on creation. Test validations for presence of email and organization. Verify the `invited_by` association works correctly.

subtasks.title: Implement Invitation Acceptance Logic
subtasks.description: Add business logic to the Invitation model to handle the process of a user accepting an invitation and becoming a member of the organization.
subtasks.details: In `app/models/invitation.rb`, create an instance method `accept!(user)`. This method should create a new `OrganizationMembership` record with the `user`, the invitation's `organization`, and the invitation's `role`. After successfully creating the membership, the invitation record should be destroyed. Add a `to_param` method that returns the `token` for use in URLs.
subtasks.testStrategy: In the Invitation model spec, add a test for the `accept!` method. Create an invitation, a user, and an organization. Call `invitation.accept!(user)` and assert that a new `OrganizationMembership` is created with the correct attributes and that the invitation record is deleted from the database.

tasks.title: Add `organization_id` Foreign Keys to Business Models
tasks.description: Create and run migrations to add an `organization_id` foreign key to all business data models that will be owned by an organization. This prepares the schema for data migration as specified in PRD tasks 2.1-2.5.
tasks.details: Generate separate migrations to add a nullable `organization_id` (type: :uuid) column with a foreign key and index to the following tables: `merchant_customers`, `merchant_products`, `merchant_invoices`, `platform_transactions`, and `custom_platform_fees`. In each corresponding model, update the `belongs_to` association from `:user` to `:organization`.
tasks.testStrategy: After running migrations, verify the schema changes in `schema.rb`. Update existing model tests to reflect the new `belongs_to :organization` association. Ensure factories are updated to create records with an associated organization, and that tests for model logic still pass.

tasks.title: Migrate Pay Gem Models to Organization Ownership
tasks.description: Update the polymorphic `owner` association for the `pay` gem's Customer and Merchant models from `User` to `Organization`. This is critical for associating subscriptions and Stripe Connect accounts with tenants instead of individual users (PRD tasks 2.6, 2.7).
tasks.details: Add `pay_customer` and `pay_merchant` method calls to the `Organization` model. Create a data migration to find all `pay_customers` and `pay_merchants` currently owned by a `User` and update their `owner_type` to 'Organization' and `owner_id` to the ID of the user's newly created default organization.
tasks.testStrategy: Write integration tests for subscription creation and Stripe Connect onboarding flows, ensuring the `Pay::Customer` and `Pay::Merchant` records are correctly associated with an `Organization` instance. Test that existing subscription data can be correctly accessed after the data migration.

tasks.title: Backfill Data and Enforce Schema Constraints
tasks.description: Create and run a data migration script to populate the new `organization_id` columns for all existing data. After successful backfilling, add NOT NULL constraints to enforce the new data model (PRD tasks 2.8, 2.9).
tasks.details: Create a Rails data migration (`db/data/`). The script should iterate through each `User`, create a default `Organization` (e.g., "John Doe's Team"), create an `OrganizationMembership` with the 'owner' role, and then update all of that user's associated records (`merchant_products`, etc.) with the new organization's ID. Create a subsequent schema migration to add `null: false` constraints to all `organization_id` columns and remove the now-redundant `user_id` columns.
tasks.testStrategy: Test the migration script thoroughly on a staging environment with a production data dump. Write assertions within the migration to verify data integrity post-execution. After the migration, run the full RSpec test suite to ensure no regressions have been introduced.

tasks.title: Implement Organization Context and Authorization
tasks.description: Implement the application's request-level context to manage the current organization and create controller concerns for authorization based on a user's role within that organization (PRD Phase 3).
tasks.details: Add `organization` and `membership` attributes to `app/models/current.rb`. Create an `OrganizationContext` concern with a `before_action` to set `Current.organization` from a session variable (`session[:current_organization_id]`). Create an `OrganizationAuthorization` concern with methods like `require_organization_admin` and `require_organization_owner`. Include these concerns in `ApplicationController`.
tasks.testStrategy: Write request specs to test the context-setting logic, including redirection when no context is set. Write controller tests for a sample controller to verify that the authorization methods correctly grant or deny access based on the user's role in `Current.organization`.

tasks.title: Implement UI Organization Switcher and Management
tasks.description: Create the primary UI components for multi-tenancy: an organization switcher in the navbar and the controllers/views for users to manage their organizations (PRD tasks 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.7).
tasks.details: Create a `_organization_switcher.html.erb` partial rendered in the navbar, powered by a Stimulus controller. The 'Switch' action should POST to a new `OrganizationsController#switch` action, which updates the session and redirects. Generate the `OrganizationsController` with standard RESTful actions (index, new, create, show) and corresponding views styled with Tailwind CSS.
tasks.testStrategy: Write a system test where a user belonging to two organizations can see both in the dropdown, switch context, and see the page content update accordingly. Write controller tests for `OrganizationsController` to verify authorization and correct behavior for each action.

tasks.title: Implement Team Member and Invitation Management UI
tasks.description: Develop the UI for organization admins to invite new members via email, manage the roles of existing members, and remove members from an organization (PRD tasks 4.5, 4.6).
tasks.details: Create `OrganizationMembersController` and `OrganizationInvitationsController` nested under the `organizations` resource. Implement logic for sending invitation emails using Action Mailer with a tokenized link. Create views for listing members, changing roles via a form, and managing pending/revoking invitations. The invitation acceptance page should handle both new user sign-ups and existing user logins.
tasks.testStrategy: Write a system test for the full invitation flow: an admin sends an invite, the recipient receives the email, clicks the link, signs up/logs in, and is successfully added to the organization. Test role changes and member removal. Use `assert_enqueued_email_with` to test email delivery.

tasks.title: Refactor Controllers and Services for Organization Scope
tasks.description: Update all existing business logic in controllers and services to operate within the scope of the `Current.organization` instead of `Current.user`. This is a major refactoring to make the application tenant-aware (PRD Phases 5 & 6).
tasks.details: Systematically refactor controllers like `MerchantProductsController`, `MerchantCustomersController`, and `MerchantInvoicesController`. Replace all instances of `Current.user.products` with `Current.organization.products`, etc. Update services like `InvoiceService` and `ProductSyncService` to accept an organization object. Move subscription and Stripe Connect logic (e.g., `subscribed?`, `can_accept_payments?`) from the `User` model to the `Organization` model.
tasks.testStrategy: This is a refactoring task, so the existing test suite is critical. Update all relevant controller and service tests to first establish an organization context (e.g., `Current.organization = organization`). Add new tests to explicitly check for data scoping, ensuring a user from Org A cannot access data from Org B through any controller action.

tasks.title: Implement Organization Settings and Billing Management
tasks.description: Create a dedicated, multi-tabbed settings page for organizations, allowing admins to manage general settings, billing/subscription, and Stripe Connect onboarding (PRD task 4.4).
tasks.details: Extend the `OrganizationsController` with `edit` and `update` actions. Create an `app/views/organizations/edit.html.erb` view with a tabbed layout. The 'General' tab will manage name/slug. The 'Billing' tab will link to the Pay gem's billing portal for the organization. The 'Stripe Connect' tab will show onboarding status and link to the Connect onboarding flow, now associated with the organization.
tasks.testStrategy: Write system tests for an organization admin navigating to the settings page. Test that they can successfully update the organization's name. Test that the billing and Stripe Connect links are correctly generated for the organization context. Verify that non-admin members cannot access this page.

tasks.title: Finalize Routing, Navigation, and Onboarding
tasks.description: Update all application routing and navigation to be organization-centric. Implement an onboarding flow for a user's first organization to ensure a smooth setup experience (PRD Phase 8).
tasks.details: In `config/routes.rb`, nest all merchant-facing resources under an organization scope (e.g., `resources :organizations do resources :products end`). Update the `sidebar_helper.rb` and other navigation partials to generate links that include the `Current.organization`. Create an onboarding flow that, after a user's first sign-up, prompts them to create their first organization and sets it as their current context.
tasks.testStrategy: Write request specs to ensure old, non-nested routes are properly redirected or return a 404, and that new nested routes are correctly protected by organization membership authorization. Write a system test for the new user sign-up and onboarding flow, verifying they are guided to create an organization and land on the dashboard with the correct context set.
